biography.background:
Thirak est un Saurak Marine "Marksman". Elle sait utiliser toutes les armes et en garde un véritable arsenal sur elle, mais est spécialisée dans les attaques à distance. Les "hommes-lézards" étant habitués à la guerre, il sait que pour surprendre et vaincre ses ennemis, il faut rester mobile en permanence.

Comment jouer Thirak ?

  • Un Saurak fort sait ignorer le Stress et ne se laisse pas facilement repousser.

  • Vos connaissance sur la guerre vous donnent un @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.0Z4aY5QLxjwyOFs0]{Avantage Tactique} permettant de contrôler vos ennemis ou leur infliger une grande quantité de dégâts.

  • Positionnez-vous et faites des tirs de couverture avec @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.BAMxbwo6xrJ1BIen]{Suppressing Fire} pour imposer un désavantage à vos adversaires !

  • Votre @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.lppq3objCi9orUKZ]{Combat Expertise} permet d'ajouter des dés de dégâts supplémentaires quelques fois par session.

  • Enfin, si cela ne suffit pas, relancez les 1 et les 2 sur vos dés de dégâts !

system.description:
Spend 3 Hope after you succeed on a weapon attack to choose one:

  • Press the Attack: Add a number of damage dice equal to your Proficiency to the damage roll.

  • Suppress: The target must mark 2 Stress.

  • Break Formation: Move the target to another point within Close range of its current position.

You can carry up to four additional weapons in your inventory instead of two.

Additionally, you can swap one of your active weapons with another weapon in your inventory without marking Stress.

When you make a weapon attack, you can choose to gain +1 to your Proficiency for that attack's damage roll.

You can do this a number of times per session equal to your Proficiency.

A Marine is a weapon specialist capable of transporting and using a variety of weapons efficiently. In combat, alternate between your weapons to deal the most damage you can or help your allies. You will also be very stylish doing so.

Note: start the game with 4 weapons instead of 2.
Once per Long Rest, when you would mark a Stress, you may ignore it.
Once per Long Rest, ignore being moved or knocked Prone.
Once per session, when an attack would cause you to mark a Stress, you can spend a Hope instead.

When you successfully attack an adversary with a weapon beyond Melee range, you can mark a Stress to temporarily Suppress them or until the end of their next Spotlight.

While an adversary is Suppressed, they have disadvantage to making an attack against a creature other than you.

When an ally within your weapon's range is attacked by an adversary you can see that is also within range, you can mark a Stress to make a weapon attack against that adversary as a Reaction.

If you succeed, choose one:

  • The attack against your ally is made with disadvantage.

  • The ally can move anywhere within Close range.

  • The adversary becomes Vulnerable.

When you succeed on a ranged weapon attack with Hope, you can choose one additional creature within the weapon's range. That creature must mark a Stress and an ally within Melee range of that creature can gain a Hope.

Additionally, once per scene, you no longer need to mark Stress to use @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.BAMxbwo6xrJ1BIen]{Suppressing Fire} or @UUID[Compendium.daggerheart-scifi-content.character-options.aQxAhZ9GcjHhYRyv]{Covering Fire}.

system.description: Powerful reptilian warriors bred for survival and conquest. Sauraks stand up to 7 feet tall, are generally muscular, and are covered in tough, scaly skin. Spiky horns grow from their skulls and form bony “beards” along their jaws that sometimes extend down their spines to their powerful tails.
Being part of a warborne community means you come from a place that is, or was, ravaged by war.
